text.title: Design System Governance Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether independent parties actually contend over the system — external consuming teams, inbound contributions, and referenceable deprecation policy — to decide between skipping, a reduced ownership-only model, and the full RFC pipeline.

decision-tree.root-question: How many independent parties does a system decision bind — teams outside the maintainer's own repository whose work a token rename or component change would break?

branch.when: one contributor, one repository, no consuming team outside it

conclusion.verdict: skip; there is no contention to resolve, so the RFC pipeline becomes paperwork filed against yourself — revisit when a second consuming team appears

branch.when: nothing is published or versioned yet — there is no release for anyone to depend on

conclusion.verdict: skip; establish a release and version scheme first, and use design-system-impact-queue to capture system implications meanwhile

branch.when: two or more consuming teams depend on published, versioned artefacts
branch.question: Do the consuming teams submit changes themselves, or does the core team make every change while outsiders only file requests?

branch.when: the core team makes every change; outsiders file requests and never open a PR

conclusion.verdict: apply the reduced model: one named owner per pillar plus an escalation chain ending in one person; defer the RFC pipeline and review SLA until inbound PRs exist

branch.when: outside teams open PRs against the system (federated or hybrid)
branch.question: Do separately versioned deprecation and breaking-change policy documents already exist, so this artefact can reference them by URL plus version or commit SHA?

branch.when: no such documents exist, so their windows and timelines would have to be written into the governance artefact itself

conclusion.verdict: halt; author breaking-change-deprecation-policy first and reference it — never inline deprecation windows, removal timelines or the classification list here

branch.when: the policies exist and are referenceable, but no individual holds tie-break authority — 'the design council decides'

conclusion.verdict: halt; name the single decider and the time bound before publishing, or the first contested token rename is decided by whichever team ships a local override first

branch.when: the policies are referenceable and a single tie-break holder is named

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; mechanical RFC threshold, every pipeline stage with a dwell time and default outcome, first-response SLA published with last period's measured p50 and p90
